- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods — if recent 5–7 days show strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–4 consecutive days falling), adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5 points.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final prediction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction — align forecast with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment is trending up, forecast should rise, not fall).
